summary: Static technical audit against expand-md.js output (file has zero {{prompt:}} markers; expander passthrough is byte-identical) + four compendiums (platform_and_boundaries full 47-rule ledger, research_claims full 14-rule ledger, prompts full 47-rule ledger, pedagogy technical subset items 16/22/23/36/37). File is a pure theory/reference supplementary page: zero fenced **Prompt** blocks, zero [Skill: ...] references, zero explicit Claude Code/Anthropic platform-capability claims — this collapses the large majority of both compendiums to N/A, which the ledger enumerates rather than omits per the completeness contract. Sole citation (Simon Willison, 'The lethal trifecta', simonwillison.net, 2025-06-16) independently re-verified live (WebFetch + curl HEAD, HTTP 200): byline, date, three-leg definition, and the quoted constraint sentence all match the source verbatim. Citation carries a correct [practitioner direct] label + URL in the maintainer-block source-verification section per check_research_claims.md's own scope rule (labels live in the maintainer block, not the student-facing body); freshness stamp `[checked:2026-07-02 result:OK due:2027-01-02]` is present and arithmetically correct. The Willison ~95%-detection point is confirmed deliberately number-free in body, avoiding a zombie-stat shape. Registry cross-check: 'the-lethal-trifecta' is present in site/layouts/curriculum.js's ae101 supplementaries list tagged '// M3', matching the file's own maintainer-block placement claim; the M3 file it names (earn-the-trust.md) independently confirmed to actually use the access-control-analysis/STRIDE skills this page's mechanism bullet references. Two non-blocking findings, both worth the author's read: (1) the cited framework is 13 months old at audit time — past the compendium's 6-month freshness window — and, unlike this same training's ironies-of-automation.md (which explicitly opens 'This is a 1983 result, not an AI take' to date its Bainbridge citation inline), this file's body never states the Willison piece's date; only the maintainer block does. (2) the maintainer block calls this page's cross-file wiring an 'unavoidable pre-leash beat' / 'the last mandatory beat before the send-off prompt', but in both host files (earn-the-trust.md ## Next; run-the-first-experiment.md ## Send the task off) the three-question check is delivered as body prose ahead of the next {{prompt:}} fence, never encoded inside a prompt block itself — a prompt-only reader can paste past it. Neither finding is blocking; no platform-capability claim, skill reference, or URL failed independent verification. Top-level verdict PASS.
